Panthers skipper Isaah Yeo left the field in the first half at Go Media Stadium on Friday night with a suspected pectoral injury.
Yeo went in to make a tackle and immediately reached for his shoulder and had a shocked look on his face as he reeled away.
The NSW and Australian captain left the field in the 34th minute and cut a forlorn figure on the Panthers bench in the second term. He will be sent for scans to confirm the severity of the injury.
Before the game, Panthers centre Casey McLean had surgery on a fractured hand but is expected to miss only 1-2 matches.
McLean suffered the injury during Saturday's game against the Raiders in Mudgee and left the field with 20 minutes to play.
The injury to McLean saw three-time premiership winner Izack Tago promoted to the starting side for Friday night's bumper clash with the Warriors.
In Friday's second game, Roosters fullback James Tedesco missed the Round 23 blockbuster against the Bulldogs after failing to overcome an ankle injury.
Tedesco sat out the second half of the Round 22 slaughter of the Cowboys with ice on his ankle but he was initially named to return against the Bulldogs.

NRL Match Preview: Round 23 v Dragons
The Sharks come into the Dragons derby having won 9 from their last 10 games, but are ultra-wary that they can’t let complacency creep in.
St George are on the back of 3 straight losses and languishing in last on the NRL ladder, although the Red V were in a similar position last season and stunned the Sharks with a 22-14 victory.
The local rivals have had many fierce encounters over the years playing for the Monty Porter Memorial Cup, and when you add Indigenous Round into the equation it could make for an emotional matchup.
“Sometimes it can be in a good way, and then sometimes it can be the other way,” Sharks coach Craig Fitzgibbon said.
“We didn’t perform last year. It’s the same round, Indigenous Round, round 23 last year at Kogarah. So, we didn’t perform there last year, and that stung.
“The Indigenous boys are incredibly proud of this round and to wear the jersey, and the make-up of this jersey has some significance in it, but to be fair on the boys, they all said to me individually that they just want to focus on getting the performance done and playing the way the Sharks do.”
The ever-reliable Mawene Hiroti starts in the centres for KL Iro, who is out with concussion.
Michael Gabrael is a chance to make his NRL debut, named in jumper 18 on the 6-man bench.
The 21-year-old was the equal 3rd top try scorer in NSW Cup last year; Gabrael has 26 tries and 10 try assists from his 31 games for the Newtown Jets.
“(Mawene’s) just so NRL ready and he’s going to be a huge asset for the Titans next year, and we’re going to miss him dearly,” Fitzgibbon said.
“It was a bit of a difficult call would have loved to look at Micky Gabrael there.
“He’s getting close to a debut as well, but for Mawene’s performance it is hard to ignore, and he’s an out-and-out first grader so Micky G’s time will come soon too.”
Nicho Hynes could break the record for most consecutive goal kicks in the NRL tomorrow afternoon.
Cronulla’s number 7 is on a streak of 32 straight goals, equal second all-time; needing 4 more in a row to beat Hazem El Masri’s record from 2003.
“Of course it’s on his mind,” the Sharks coach shared.
“It’s an incredible milestone for our game and for Nicho, but he’s also very process-driven at the moment and the amount of work he’s doing.
“He’s just going to trust his process and the way he kicks the ball the same way.
“It’s been building for a couple of weeks, so it’s not like this week is any different to the others because there have been little milestones along the way for him.
“I think he’s excited for the challenge and not doing anything other than trying to work hard and get better.”
His halves partner Braydon Trindall just broke the club’s most try assists in a season record, surpassing Nicho’s 2023 efforts.
There’s a record up for grabs for Ronaldo Mulitalo tomorrow too; he needs one more try to pass club legend David Peachey for the outright second most tries for the club (which will be 111).
Mulitalo has seven tries against the Dragons, while Will Kennedy has the club record of 8 tries against them.
Under Craig Fitzgibbon, the Sharks have won 8/9 Local Derbies against St George, winning their last encounter in Round 14 at Ocean Protect Stadium, with their only loss coming in Round 23 last year in Kogarah.

August 8 th 2026, 2:17am , By: Ben Bridge
Sunday afternoon at Jubilee Stadium closes the NRL Round 23 slate with the latest chapter of one of rugby league’s oldest local rivalries. The Dragons will bring emotion and home ground desperation, but this matchup should still be heavily controlled by Cronulla .
The Sharks are genuine premiership contenders and enter after a convincing 32-16 win over South Sydney, their fifth consecutive victory. The Dragons narrowly lost 28-22 to the Dolphins and remain last, with their only home win at Jubilee Stadium this season coming against the Tigers.
My fair spread is approximately Sharks -17.5, which sits close to the available market. Normally, that would point toward leaving the game alone. However, the gap between these teams is so significant that I still expect Cronulla to create separation across 80 minutes.
The Sharks are without KL Iro due to concussion and have named Mawene Hiroti in the centres. Siosifa Talakai is being rested, while the Dragons lose Toby Couchman and bring Emre Guler into the starting pack.
The rivalry is the only major reason for caution, along with possible showers. Local derbies can become physical, emotional, and far tighter than the ratings suggest. But if Cronulla remain patient, their forward pack and spine should eventually overwhelm St George Illawarra.
Dragons vs Sharks Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 23
Dragons Competitive but Still Fall Short
The Dragons’ 28-22 loss to the Dolphins was another performance that contained enough effort to avoid embarrassment but not enough polish to deliver a result. St George Illawarra remained in the contest and gave itself opportunities late, yet once again walked away without competition points.
That has become the story of their improved second half of the season. Dean Young has lifted the effort, defensive connectivity, and competitiveness of the team, but the Dragons remain limited with the ball and struggle to convert good periods into wins.
Clint Gutherson continues to provide leadership from fullback, while Damien Cook gives the side speed around the ruck. Kyle Flanagan and Daniel Atkinson have brought more organisation to the halves, however Young has dropped Atkinson to the bench in favour of youngster Lyhkan King-Togia, and it will be interesting to see what he can bring to the table this week.
The concern is what happens when opponents score quickly. The Dragons do not possess enough repeatable attacking weapons to confidently chase games. Valentine Holmes and Moses Suli can create on the edges, but the broader structure still requires high completion and favourable territory.
Toby Couchman’s absence weakens a forward pack that has been one of the few clear positives. Emre Guler has been promoted to start, joining Loko Pasifiki Tonga in the front row, while the Dragons continue to rely heavily on younger forwards through the rotation.
That is a difficult setup against Cronulla. The Sharks’ middle includes Addin Fonua-Blake, Thomas Hazelton, Cameron McInnes, and several powerful interchange options. If the Dragons lose the yardage battle, their attack may spend most of the afternoon starting from poor field position.
Jubilee Stadium has not provided meaningful protection. The Dragons average only 14 points and concede around 28 per home game this season.

Cronulla’s 32-16 win over South Sydney reinforced the view that the Sharks are now one of the competition’s most complete sides. They controlled the middle, converted attacking opportunities and extended their winning streak to five matches.
The Sharks’ attack has been outstanding throughout the past two months. NRL Round 23 is headlined by a top-four blockbuster in Auckland and Sydney Roosters’ showdown with fellow in-form outfit Canterbury Bulldogs.
Meanwhile, four Top 8 teams and a couple of fringe sides get an ideal opportunity to boost their finals prospects when they take on opponents currently languishing in the bottom seven spots.

These derby rivals lost their Round 22 home fixtures by a combined margin of 106 points – but it’s the still-in-contention Cowboys most under the microscope after last week’s historic loss.
FORM: The Titans’ followed up their first back-to-back wins of the season – scoring 38 points against both Manly and St George Illawarra – with a crushing 42-6 home loss to the Warriors.
The Cowboys are in disarray after a record-shattering 82-12 loss to the Roosters, which came on the back of a 3-1 run that included wins over the Panthers, Sea Eagles and Broncos.
INS AND OUTS: Zane Harrison’s season-ending injury sees Lachlan Ilias return in the Titans’ No.7 jersey. The Cowboys get Griffin Neame back from suspension, but Jeremiah Nanai has been ruled out with Kai O’Donnell coming in.
KEY MATCH-UP: Keano Kini tried hard in a steamrolled team last week, but fellow fullback livewire Scott Drinkwater’s passive display against the Roosters rightly came under a harsh spotlight.
HISTORY: The Cowboys have won their last three against the Titans, scoring 110 points in the process. They prevailed 30-16 in Townsville in Round 3.
KEY STAT: The Titans have won four of their last six against the Cowboys at Cbus Super Stadium, averaging 23 points across those six encounters.
Scott Drinkwater has scored five tries in his last five games against the Titans.
VERDICT: After a week of soul-searching, the Cowboys receive an ideal opportunity to reset and get their finals bid back on track. Four of 10 teams to conceded 50-plus points in 2026 have won their next game – and Todd Payten’s chastened side is still in the thick of the Top 8 race.
The Titans took a sizeable step back last week and Harrison’s injury is a bitter blow for a team that looked to be turning a corner. With both sides taking an optional attitude to defence, the over also holds plenty of appeal in this one.

Presented By
Dolphins v Broncos: Katoa ready to shine; Duffy steps up
The Dolphins will continue their chase for a top-four finish when they take on the Broncos in the latest edition of the Battle for Brisbane.
Isaiya Katoa made a successful return from a wrist injury last week to steer the Dolphins past the Dragons and they are out to keep the momentum rolling against the Broncos on Saturday night.
The Dolphins have beaten Brisbane just once since their introduction to the competition in 2023 but they are after more than just bragging rights at Suncorp Stadium this weekend.
Kristian Woolf's men sit fifth and are chasing a top-four finish as they seek a maiden finals berth.
Brisbane's chances of qualifying for the finals were extinguished with a 24-point loss to the Knights last weekend but they still have plenty to play for.
The Broncos claimed a 26-12 victory when the two sides faced off earlier this season and Michael Maguire's men would like nothing more than toppling their local rivals.
A host of stars are also pushing for a World Cup berth later this season, with Reece Walsh and Pat Carrigan among the Kangaroos contenders.

Dolphins : No further changes on game day after one change to the bench in the 24-hour update with Brian Pouniu elevated with Sebastian Su'a dropping out. Earlier, centre Jake Averillo was again listed among the reserves as he chases his first appearance since Round 19 having recovered from a rib injury. Winger Jamayne Isaako has scored nine tries in his last seven games at Suncorp Stadium.
Broncos : One change to the six-man bench 90 minutes before kick-off, with Blake Mozer coming into the 19 and Hayze Perham dropping out. A new-look spine for Michael Maguire with Billy Walters back in the starting side at hooker at the expense of Cory Paix while Thomas Duffy takes over at halfback from Adam Reynolds (concussion). Xavier Willison has been named to play despite suffering a laceration to his leg in last week's loss to the Knights. He will line up at prop, with Va'a Semu dropping to the bench.
